subject: Urgent: FluxPay latency surge - telemetry & evidence request
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fluxpay.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Martin Lopez <mlopez@fluxpay.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High-latency incidents today + request for logs / chain-of-custody

Hi Sofia,

We experienced a significant latency spike and elevated 5xx rate across the Redwood endpoint our auth service calls between 02:42–03:17 UTC today. Our execs are asking for a concise evidence packet for our risk committee and external auditors — they want:
- a time-indexed snapshot of runtime telemetry (latency histogram, error-rate by shard)
- retention window and deletion policy for the logs you’ll provide
- statement/controls about chain-of-custody and whether raw logs contain any customer data (PII)

I’m attaching a short request doc that lists the fields our auditors need. Can you confirm what we can provide and the turnaround? This is high priority; our CTO and legal are on standby.

Thanks,
Alex

[Attachment: fluxpay_request_20270606.pdf (PDF)]
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fluxpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High-latency incidents today + request for logs / chain-of-custody

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and the attachment. Sorry you ran into this. Quick summary of what we can provide immediately and next steps: 

1) What we can deliver within 24 hours:
   - time-indexed telemetry snapshot (per-minute latency histograms and 5xx counts for the affected model/route)
   - KV-cache and request routing metadata for the time window
   - a redacted sample of request/response payloads (PII redacted)

2) Retention / provenance:
   - Runtime telemetry (aggregates + non-PII traces) retained for 90 days by default; raw request logs are retained for 30 days unless a legal hold is placed.
   - We can preserve a forensics export (read-only archive) in our secure evidence S3 bucket for 180 days on request.

3) Chain-of-custody and sanitization:
   - All exported artifacts will include an export manifest, SHA256 checksums, and an access log.
   - We will run an automated redaction pass on request payloads and include redaction logs describing fields removed.

I’m looping in Sean (runtime) for the telemetry packages and Marissa (legal) to confirm the preservation workflow and any NDA/POA needs. I’ll aim to get an initial packet to you in ≈8–12 hours. If your auditors need different retention durations, tell us and we’ll escalate to preserve the artifacts.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fluxpay.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High-latency incidents today + request for logs / chain-of-custody

Sofia / Alex — adding technical detail so expectations are clear.

- We have continuous telemetry (per-host / per-model / per-route) stored as compressed aggregates. I can produce a per-minute CSV and the latency histogram JSON for 02:00–04:00 UTC.
- Raw request logs (full token-level request/response) are stored on a short retention tier; they may contain user-generated text. We will not export full raw request bodies without explicit sign-off.
- For the 02:42–03:17 window I can:
   a) export aggregated metrics + traces (no payloads) now;
   b) prepare a redacted payload sample (automatic field-level redaction + manual review) — depends on legal okay.

Technical notes: the spike correlated with a regional batch job that increased prefix reuse; we’ll include KV cache hit rates and batching window stats. Export ETA: aggregated telemetry in 4–6 hours, redacted payload sample in 10–14 hours (pending Marissa).

—Sean
Principal Reliability Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fluxpay.com>, Lawson Legal <legal@lawsonllp.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High-latency incidents today + request for logs / chain-of-custody

Alex / Sofia / team — legal here. A few points before we move raw artifacts: 

1) Custody & access: we’ll stage a read-only evidence export in s3://redwood-evidence/fluxpay/DL-7832/20270606/ with strict ACLs and an access manifest. Access requests will be recorded and require an authorized contact from FluxPay.
2) Redaction policy: redacted samples are acceptable for immediate auditor review. If FluxPay requires raw unredacted requests, we need:
   - a signed data sharing addendum (DocuSign), or
   - an executed mutual NDA + POA authorizing access to user content (we can expedite).
3) Timeline & chain-of-custody artifacts: export manifest + SHA256 checksums + a custody log (who downloaded/approved) will be included.

If FluxPay confirms they accept redacted samples for the initial review, we’ll proceed immediately. If they require unredacted artifacts, please route signed legal paperwork to legal@redwood.com and we’ll hold artifacts under legal hold.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fluxpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High-latency incidents today + request for logs / chain-of-custody

Alex — final status update: 

- Delivered: per-minute telemetry CSV + latency histogram JSON + KV cache stats for 02:00–04:00 UTC. Files staged to the secure evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/fluxpay/DL-7832/20270606/.
- Delivered attachments: runtime_telemetry_snapshot_20270606.tar.gz (manifest + checksums).
- Redacted sample: redacted_runtime_sample_20270606.json attached and included in the evidence folder. The redaction report is included and documents which fields were stripped.
- Chain-of-custody: export_manifest.json, sha256_manifest.txt, and custody_access_log.csv included in same folder.

Next steps: if FluxPay legal wants unredacted raw logs we’ll require the signed DSAA or NDA per Marissa. Otherwise, please confirm receipt and whether this packet meets the auditor’s needs; we can schedule a short exec debrief tomorrow at 10:00 PT to walk through the artifacts.

Thanks — I’ll monitor the ticket and can escalate to the incident response lead if you see gaps.

—Sofia
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: runtime_telemetry_snapshot_20270606.tar.gz, redacted_runtime_sample_20270606.json]
summary: FluxPay reported a latency and 5xx spike. Redwood provided aggregated telemetry and a redacted payload sample, staged evidence in a secure S3 location with manifest/checksums, and described chain-of-custody and legal prerequisites for unredacted logs. Legal and infra coordinated timelines and conditions for sharing raw artifacts.
